title: Does orientability matter for rationality of scl in surface groups?
body:
## The question

Let S be a closed hyperbolic surface and let C be a chain in pi_1(S): a formal sum of
cyclically reduced conjugacy classes whose total homology class is trivial. It is
conjectured that scl(C) is always rational.

Does the answer depend on whether S is orientable?

Two readings, and both are open. Does rationality hold for closed non-orientable
hyperbolic surfaces as well as orientable ones? And would a proof of the orientable case
transfer, or is there some argument that uses orientability essentially?

It is not clear that it should matter. It is recorded separately because a proof of the
orientable case that leaned on orientability would leave the general statement open, and
it would be easy not to notice that at the time.
author: danny
